# Generated curl configuration

`curl_config.h` in each platform directory was produced **once** by curl's own
CMake and committed. It is not hand-written and should not be hand-edited.

## Why generated-and-committed

curl has roughly 200 interdependent feature defines: disabling one obliges you
not to reference another, and the `HAVE_*` probes are genuine compile-and-link
tests against the target's headers. Deriving that by hand from `addCMacro`
calls is a good way to produce a curl that compiles and then misbehaves.

The two alternatives were worse:

- **Hand-derive the defines.** Error-prone for the reason above.
- **Run curl's CMake at build time** (a `b.addSystemCommand` step). That
  reintroduces CMake as a build dependency — the thing this repo's migration
  removed — and leaves cross-compilation as awkward as it was, since CMake
  would need its own toolchain file to target anything but the host.

Generating once and committing keeps the config machine-produced *and* the
build pure Zig, so `zig build -Dtarget=...` still works.

## Regenerating

Needs CMake and a built mbedtls, and is only necessary when bumping curl or
changing the feature set.

```sh
# 1. mbedtls, which curl's configure needs to find.
#    -DMBEDTLS_FATAL_WARNINGS=OFF because mbedtls 3.6.2 trips
#    -Wunterminated-string-initialization on current clang and makes it fatal.
#    Its `framework` submodule is required even with testing off, and
#    `zig fetch` does not fetch submodules, so clone it in first.
cmake -S <mbedtls> -B mbedbuild -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DENABLE_TESTING=OFF -DENABLE_PROGRAMS=OFF \
  -DUSE_SHARED_MBEDTLS_LIBRARY=OFF -DMBEDTLS_FATAL_WARNINGS=OFF \
  -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=mbedinst
cmake --build mbedbuild -j8 && cmake --install mbedbuild

# 2. curl, configure only — the artifacts are discarded, only the header is kept.
cmake -S <curl> -B curlbuild \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DBUILD_STATIC_LIBS=ON \
  -DBUILD_CURL_EXE=OFF -DBUILD_TESTING=OFF -DBUILD_EXAMPLES=OFF \
  -DCURL_USE_MBEDTLS=ON -DCURL_USE_OPENSSL=OFF \
  -DCURL_USE_LIBSSH2=OFF -DCURL_USE_LIBSSH=OFF -DCURL_USE_LIBPSL=OFF \
  -DUSE_LIBIDN2=OFF -DCURL_USE_GSSAPI=OFF \
  -DCURL_BROTLI=OFF -DCURL_ZSTD=OFF \
  -DCURL_ZLIB=ON -DUSE_NGHTTP2=ON \
  -DCURL_DISABLE_LDAP=ON -DCURL_DISABLE_LDAPS=ON -DCURL_DISABLE_FTP=ON \
  -DCURL_DISABLE_TELNET=ON -DCURL_DISABLE_DICT=ON -DCURL_DISABLE_TFTP=ON \
  -DCURL_DISABLE_GOPHER=ON -DCURL_DISABLE_IMAP=ON -DCURL_DISABLE_POP3=ON \
  -DCURL_DISABLE_SMTP=ON -DCURL_DISABLE_SMB=ON -DCURL_DISABLE_RTSP=ON \
  -DCURL_DISABLE_MQTT=ON -DCURL_DISABLE_FILE=ON -DCURL_DISABLE_NTLM=ON \
  -DMBEDTLS_INCLUDE_DIRS=mbedinst/include \
  -DMBEDTLS_LIBRARY=mbedinst/lib/libmbedtls.a \
  -DMBEDX509_LIBRARY=mbedinst/lib/libmbedx509.a \
  -DMBEDCRYPTO_LIBRARY=mbedinst/lib/libmbedcrypto.a \
  -DNGHTTP2_INCLUDE_DIR=nginst/include -DNGHTTP2_LIBRARY=nginst/lib/libnghttp2.a \
  -DZLIB_INCLUDE_DIR=zlinst/include -DZLIB_LIBRARY=zlinst/lib/libz.a

cp curlbuild/lib/curl_config.h third_party/curl_config/<platform>/
```

Confirm the summary curl prints matches what is intended:

    Protocols: http https ipfs ipns ws wss
    Features:  alt-svc AsynchDNS HSTS HTTP2 HTTPS-proxy IPv6 Largefile libz
               SSL threadsafe UnixSockets
    Enabled SSL backends: mbedTLS

## Feature choices

**Kept.** Proxy support, because it is a documented `bh_http_config` option
with its own tests. IPv6. Unix sockets. HSTS and alt-svc, which come along
with HTTP and cost nothing.

**Dropped.** FTP, LDAP/LDAPS, SMTP, IMAP, POP3, SMB, RTSP, MQTT, telnet, dict,
gopher, tftp, file, NTLM. None reachable through this extension's API, and each
is attack surface in a library whose whole job is parsing hostile input.

**GSS-API off, deliberately.** SPNEGO tokens are generated by
`src/negotiate_auth.cpp` via `dlopen`, not by curl, so `CURLAUTH_NEGOTIATE` is
never used. Leaving it off also avoids statically linking MIT Kerberos, which
reads `/etc/krb5.conf` and `dlopen`s its own plugins — so it would not really
be static anyway.

**No HTTP/3.** It requires a QUIC-capable TLS library; curl's CMake fails with
"ngtcp2 requires OpenSSL, wolfSSL or GnuTLS". mbedTLS cannot do it, so HTTP/3
and matching DuckDB's TLS stack are mutually exclusive.

**HTTP/2 and zlib are in.** nghttp2 because multiplexing is what the batch
fan-out wants — verified negotiating `HTTP/2 200` against cloudflare.com — and
zlib because most APIs serve compressed and it is small. zlib's `gz*.c` are
omitted: that is the stdio gzFile API, which curl does not use.

Both need their own generated headers, captured the same way:
`nghttp2_config/config.h`, `nghttp2_config/nghttp2/nghttp2ver.h`,
`zlib_config/zconf.h`.

## Platforms

Only `macos_arm64` so far. Each target needs its own, generated on (or
cross-configured for) that platform, because the `HAVE_*` probes really do
differ. Cross-compiling to a target without a committed config will fail at the
include, which is the right failure — loud, and at build time.
